segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the fifth angel blew his trumpet, and I saw a star that had fallen from the sky to the earth, and the key to the shaft of the abyss was given to him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He opened the shaft of the abyss, and smoke rose out of the shaft like the smoke of a great furnace, and the sun and the air were darkened by the smoke from the shaft.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And out of the smoke locusts came onto the earth, and power was given to them like the power that the scorpions of the earth have.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They were told not to harm the grass of the earth or any green plant or any tree, but only the people who do not have the seal of God on their foreheads.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They were not allowed to kill them, but only to torment them for five months; and their torment was like the torment of a scorpion when it stings a person.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In those days people will seek death and will not find it; they will long to die, and death flees from them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In appearance the locusts were like horses prepared for battle. On their heads was something like crowns that looked like gold, and their faces were like human faces;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: they had hair like women’s hair, and their teeth were like lions’ teeth;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: they had breastplates like breastplates of iron, and the sound of their wings was like the sound of chariots with many horses charging into battle.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They have tails like scorpions, with stingers, and in their tails is their power to harm people for five months.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They have as king over them the angel of the abyss; his name in Hebrew is Abaddon, and in Greek he has the name Apollyon.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The first woe has passed; look, two woes are still coming after this.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the sixth angel blew his trumpet, and I heard a single voice from the horns of the golden altar that is before God,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: saying to the sixth angel, the one who had the trumpet,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Release the four angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the four angels were released, who had been prepared for that hour and day and month and year, to kill a third of humanity.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The number of the cavalry troops was twice ten thousand times ten thousand; I heard their number.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And this is how I saw the horses in the vision, and those seated on them: they had breastplates of fiery red, dark blue, and sulfur yellow. The heads of the horses were like lions’ heads, and out of their mouths come fire and smoke and sulfur.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: By these three plagues a third of humanity was killed, by the fire and the smoke and the sulfur coming out of their mouths.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For the power of the horses is in their mouths and in their tails; for their tails are like snakes, having heads, and with them they do harm.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the rest of humanity, those who were not killed by these plagues, did not turn back from the works of their hands so as to stop worshiping the demons and the idols of gold and silver and bronze and stone and wood, which can neither see nor hear nor walk;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and they did not turn back from their murders or their sorceries or their sexual immorality or their thefts.

notes.note: In Jewish writing of the period, stars often stand for heavenly beings, and this one acts as a person: it receives a key and opens the shaft. The Greek pronoun can be read as "it" or "him"; "him" is used because the star acts as an agent. Whether this figure is a fallen, evil being or simply an angel sent down from heaven is disputed.

The older English rendering "the bottomless pit" merges two Greek words: one for a well or shaft, and "abyss." In the Greek Old Testament "abyss" is the primeval deep, and by the first century it also named the underground prison of hostile spirits. The picture is of a locked shaft leading down into that realm; several modern translations render it similarly.

The Greek word normally means a wreath of the kind awarded to victors or worn at festivals, though it could also be made of gold and worn by rulers. Revelation uses a different word for the royal diadem. The hedged wording ("something like... that looked like gold") is the author's own: the vision is described by comparison throughout.

Abaddon is a Hebrew word meaning "destruction," used in the Old Testament as a name for the realm of the dead alongside Sheol. Here it is the name of a person, and the Greek equivalent given, Apollyon, means "Destroyer." Some scholars also hear an echo of the god Apollo's name, but this is uncertain.

Many manuscripts read "the four horns of the golden altar," and a number of translations follow them. Other early witnesses lack "four," and the SBLGNT text translated here omits it. The meaning is not affected, since an Israelite altar had a horn at each of its four corners.

In the Old Testament the Euphrates was the far boundary of the promised land and the direction from which invading empires such as Assyria and Babylon came. In the first century it was also the eastern frontier of the Roman empire, beyond which lay the Parthians, renowned for their cavalry. A first-century reader would have heard an invasion from the east in this image.

notes.phrase: twice ten thousand times ten thousand
notes.note: The Greek is literally "two myriads of myriads," a myriad being ten thousand, which comes to two hundred million; some translations give the figure outright. The phrasing echoes Old Testament language for countless heavenly hosts (as in Daniel 7:10) and was probably heard as an overwhelming number rather than a precise count.

The Greek word names the color of the hyacinth, a dark blue or violet, and is used in the Greek Old Testament for blue-dyed cloth. The three colors of the breastplates match the fire, smoke and sulfur that come from the horses' mouths, the dark blue answering to the smoke. The Greek could mean that the horses as well as the riders wear the breastplates.

The traditional rendering is "repent," which most translations keep as an established term understood to include a change of life. In current English, however, "repent" centers on feeling sorry, whereas the Greek word carries the prophets' call to return to God: a change of direction in mind and conduct. Here the sense is that the survivors did not abandon their idols and their crimes.

The Greek word means drugs or potions, and by extension the charms and spells of magical practice; it could also mean poisons, which would suit its place next to "murders." Most translations take it as magic in general, and that is followed here. Some manuscripts have a closely related noun that names the practice of sorcery more directly.

candidates.reason: It varies between "authority," "power" and "right" across translations and recurs throughout the New Testament; readers should be able to tell it apart from δύναμις.
It is rendered "bottomless pit," "Abyss," or "the deep" in Luke 8:31, Romans 10:7 and seven times in Revelation, and should be recognisably the same place.
It means a victor's or festal wreath as distinct from the royal διάδημα; the two need to be kept apart consistently in Paul, James, 1 Peter and Revelation.
It ranges from bowing before a superior to worship of God, and the choice between "worship," "bow down" and "pay homage" has theological weight across the Gospels and Revelation.
It is rendered "fornication," "sexual immorality," or "prostitution" in different translations, and it recurs in vice lists and as a metaphor for idolatry in Revelation.
